LunexStealer uses PDB-guided BYOVD via a vulnerable AMD driver (CVE-2023-20598) to silently blind endpoint security before stealing credentials and planting a persistent Native Messaging Host on Ukrainian 🇺🇦 targets.  Key findings:  - The infection chain starts with a fake CAPTCHA page on uasputnik[.]com, which instructs victims to run an msiexec command that silently installs a malicious MSI from %LOCALAPPDATA%, no admin required at first. LunexLoader then fakes a trusted Windows binary via PEB manipulation, abuses the CMSTPLUA COM object for UAC bypass, and installs AMD's PDFWKRNL.sys (CVE-2023-20598) as a service, gaining kernel read/write through exposed IOCTL calls, all before the stealer touches disk.  - The BYOVD implementation is unusually surgical. LunexLoader reads the victim's ntoskrnl.exe, extracts the PDB GUID for the running kernel build, and pulls matching symbols from Microsoft's Symbol Server using curl.exe. It then parses the PDB to resolve exact offsets for process, thread, and image-load callback tables, making the technique version-agnostic across Windows 10 and 11. It zeros callback entries belonging to a 20-entry blocklist that includes Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, ESET, Elastic, Kaspersky, Dr[.]Web, Sysmon, and Windows Filter Manager. Targeting Filter Manager can disable entire classes of minifilter-based products at once. Validated testing found that neither HVCI nor the then-current Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist blocked the specific PDFWKRNL.sys variant used.  - LunexStealer targets Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Yandex Browser, Opera, Opera GX, and Vivaldi, pulling credentials, cookies, tokens, and card data. It handles Chrome App-Bound Encryption and ChaCha20-Poly1305 (versions 10, 11, and 20). Crypto wallet targets include Bitcoin Core, Litecoin, Exodus, Atomic Wallet, Electrum, MetaMask, OKX Wallet, and SafePal Wallet.  - Persistence is layered: a registry Run key, a hidden scheduled task named psychedelicloveUtils, and Chrome and Edge Native Messaging Host registrations under the name com.lunex.explorer. The Native Messaging Host embeds PowerShell capable of drive enumeration, directory listing, file read/write, file download, and arbitrary execution. Ontinue confirmed it survives deletion of the stealer binary, reboots, and browser restarts, meaning removing LunexStealer.exe is not remediation.  - Ontinue identified 28 Lunex panels across 13 countries and assesses the platform as a Russian-speaking MaaS operation with CIS alignment, sold to independent criminal operators. The "Psychedelic" operator tag appears in the scheduled task name psychedelicloveUtils. Three samples are confirmed associated with this activity: bf14cd6c3328ebd08e940478b5d1da04e9e5aa576d045d41950bf4f1e2456dd8, 6e8b49cf70bf854e8c59c7d27cefa89406caf8978461190dabb86dafcd8554e1, and 06f434695f93d7fd11eeff71358ff69fed79d310a66d993bbcc4ff979c117c90.  Responder takeaway: Do not treat a live EDR process as proof of functioning visibility after a BYOVD incident. Hunt for curl.exe contacting Microsoft's Symbol Server, PDFWKRNL.sys loaded as a service, and the Native Messaging Host registry entries for com.lunex.explorer in both HKCU and HKLM Chrome and Edge NativeMessagingHosts keys. Check for a scheduled task named psychedelicloveUtils. On any system where LunexLoader ran, assume kernel callbacks may have been zeroed and validate telemetry coverage independently before trusting endpoint logs from that window.  #DFIR_Radar

There is a quiet market where old, unpatched software gets a second life as someone else's attack tool, and this week we watched a group do exactly that with a flaw from 2017.  We've been tracking Blacknet-00 a.k.a. "Infrastructure Destruction Squad" (IDS) for months. The newest listing from this group, posted October 1, is a tool for an Apache Struts vulnerability, CVE-2017-5638, the same class of bug behind several of the largest breaches of the last decade. A single crafted web request runs on the server with no login required, and the sales post walks through what the tool claims to do once it is in, confirming it has full privileges, reading sensitive system and authentication files, pulling database credentials, dropping a file to stay persistent, and opening a backdoor for later.  A few days later the same actor claimed to have used the tool against four servers, and offered both the access and the tool for sale. We have not verified that claim, but it fits a pattern we run into constantly, an old vulnerability nobody closed quietly turned into a resale opportunity.  How is a nine-year-old flaw is still a sellable product in 2026? It means these systems are still out there exposed. If you are not certain whether you have internet-facing software this old still running, that uncertainty is the gap worth closing now rather than after someone else finds it.  This is one piece of a full Blacknet-00 ransomware threat actor profile Barricade Cyber is publishing next week, where we break down the group's real toolset, a SCADA attack tool, a scanner, and their ransomware, analyzed from code we obtained.  Stay tuned to our socials and blog for more info.  #threatintel #ransomware #vulnerabilitymanagement #dfir

BREAKING: BANDIT IS HOME — OVERWHELMING PUBLIC SUPPORT HELPS REUNITE POSSUM CREEK FAMILY WITH PET RACCOON Wildlife officials reverse course after massive community response, agree to work with Miller family on proper permits By Martha Wilkins | Staff Reporter POSSUM CREEK — Bandit is back where the Miller family says he belongs. Just days after the Possum Creek Times Reporter shared the story of the beloved house-raised raccoon being removed from the Miller home following a bizarre yard sale incident, wildlife officials have agreed to return Bandit to the family while working with them to obtain the proper permits and meet the requirements necessary to legally keep him. And according to both the Millers and officials involved in the case, the overwhelming public response played a major role. Thousands of readers commented, shared the story and demanded that officials reconsider the plan to release Bandit into the wild after nearly two years of living inside the Miller home alongside the family’s two cats. The Millers received the call Thursday afternoon. Bandit was coming home. “I started crying before they even finished the sentence,” Mrs. Miller said. “I honestly thought we were never going to see him again. He came through that door, climbed right up on the couch like nothing ever happened and immediately tried to steal a snack. That’s our Bandit.” The original controversy began after Bandit crawled beneath a table during the family’s yard sale and grabbed a customer’s leg in what the Millers described as an attempt to play. The startled customer kicked Bandit, sending the raccoon into another shopper and prompting calls to local police and Animal Control. Authorities later discovered the Millers did not have the required permit to possess the raccoon. Bandit was seized, and officials initially planned to release him into the wild. That decision sparked immediate backlash. Readers argued that a raccoon raised inside a home since infancy — sleeping on furniture, eating alongside house cats and regularly using a litter box — was poorly prepared to suddenly survive on his own. According to the wildlife officer handling the case, those concerns were heard. “The public response was significant, and frankly, it caused everyone involved to take another look at the circumstances,” Game Warden Daniel Hensley said. “Our responsibility is to protect wildlife, but we also have to consider the welfare of the individual animal. Bandit is clearly not a typical wild raccoon at this point.” Hensley said officials will now work directly with the Miller family to determine what permits, enclosure requirements, veterinary documentation and other conditions must be met for Bandit to remain with them legally. “This isn’t us ignoring the law,” Hensley said. “It’s us finding a lawful solution that makes sense for the animal and the family. The Millers have been cooperative from the beginning, and we believe giving them an opportunity to come into compliance is the appropriate path forward.” Mrs. Miller said the family has agreed to every requirement presented so far. “We’ll build whatever they want us to build. We’ll fill out every form. We’ll pay every fee,” she said. “If they tell me Bandit needs his own bedroom with a fire exit and a tiny raccoon attorney, we’ll figure it out.” Bandit reportedly spent his first night home exactly where everyone expected. On the couch. Between the cats. The Miller family also asked the Possum Creek Times Reporter to pass along a message to everyone who commented, shared, called and spoke up after the original story. “You all did this,” Mrs. Miller said. “People we’ve never met cared enough about Bandit to speak up for him. We truly believe if nobody had said anything, he would have been released. We will never forget what this community did for our family.” For once, the comment section didn’t just argue. It changed something. And tonight in Possum Creek, Bandit is home.  WELCOME HOME, BANDIT. To everyone who commented, shared the original story and spoke up: this one belongs to you. #welcomeback #Heartwarming #smalltownliving #everyone

Coming up for air now after a very dense excellent week in Seoul at KBW, while staying on top of our response to a security event affecting part of our infrastructure.   I can now respond to queries and speculation regarding what is impacted and what is not affected.  Based on our investigation to date, there is no indication that MetaMask wallets or customer funds in wallets have been affected. Your Secret Recovery Phrase, your keys, and the assets in your wallet were not part of this incident because they CANNOT be. You custody and control your own keys. That is how self custody works. You are fully in control of your own money in MetaMask.  Like many providers in our industry, we constantly face attempted attacks from a range of threat actors and periodically encounter security issues. Our approach follows established best practice: we do not publicly discuss the details of an open incident, but we disclose promptly to partners and relevant stakeholders once an issue is sufficiently understood. In this case, we shared the relevant details with partners, agreed and implemented a response strategy together, and then disclosed publicly.  As a precaution, we and our partners rotated validator keys. That step is operationally inconvenient which is regrettable as validators must exit the staking queue and then re-enter the queue to restake, which takes time.   The validator staking architecture of Ethereum separates the key that proposes and attests from the key that can withdraw the stake. In accordance with the Ethereum principle of self-custody, we do not hold withdrawal keys for our clients. Because of that separation, an issue in the validator infrastructure CANNOT result in the improper movement of the underlying ETH. Rotating those keys was how we reduced residual operational risk.  Self-custody and user control are a central design principle guiding how we build -- in MetaMask, in staking and validation, and across Ethereum more broadly. Self custody plus rigorous decentralization represents a paradigm shift in security. Increasingly, the world is waking up to the benefits of this sounder architecture.

sample_tweets.text: 🇺🇸 🔻The Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (R&E), through the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies (CT), has announced an agreement to partner with the Central Intelligence Agency and In-Q-Tel (IQT), a not-for-profit strategic investor that has served the national security community since 1999.  The partnership gives the Department's research and engineering enterprise structured access to IQT's global technology-scouting platform and its portfolio of early-stage companies, with the explicit objective of compressing the timeline to transition and rapidly field mature commercial solutions from non-traditional performers to the warfighter.  The Department of War has mandated six Critical Technology Areas (CTAs) as the focus of its investment and transition efforts: Applied Artificial Intelligence, Biomanufacturing, Contested Logistics Technologies, Quantum and Battlefield Information Dominance, Scaled Directed Energy, and Scaled Hypersonics. Under the agreement, IQT will conduct technology scouting and technical due diligence across all six CTAs, as well as across enabling technology areas, while the Department identifies transition sponsors and pathways for validated technologies.  "In a contested global threat environment, technological superiority will not be determined by who invents a capability first, but by who delivers it to the warfighter fastest. The Department is fundamentally shifting its posture: we are moving from acting solely as a long-cycle technology developer to operating as an agile, credible, and rapid customer for America's most innovative non-traditional performers. Our partnership with In-Q-Tel eliminates bureaucratic friction across our six CTAs. Over the next 12 months, our benchmark for success is simple and unambiguous: moving validated commercial prototypes out of the lab and into active operational field evaluations with our combatant commands," said Hon. Michael Dodd, Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies.

Every communist state that has ever existed faced the same fatal paradox: the party that promised to liberate the people from the oppressive state ended up building the most oppressive state in human history. This occurred not because communism attracted uniquely evil people, but because the ideology itself demanded the erasure of the line between party and state; once that line was erased, the machinery of governance became a machinery of control from which no society has ever peacefully recovered.  The deep state, a term now thrown around loosely in Western democracies to describe entrenched bureaucratic interests, was not an accident or a corruption of communism. It was communism's central organising principle. Every communist regime, from Moscow to Havana to Pyongyang, deliberately and systematically fused the party with every institution of the state until the two became indistinguishable. Understanding how they did it, and why it destroyed them, is not an exercise in Cold War nostalgia. It is a warning to every country where a ruling party with an overwhelming mandate begins to treat the state as its private property.  The Soviet Union under Lenin and Stalin created the template that every subsequent communist state would follow. The process was methodical and proceeded in identifiable stages.  First, the party captured the security apparatus. The Cheka, later the OGPU, the NKVD, and finally the KGB, was not a state institution that served the republic. It was a party organ that served the Politburo. Its officers were selected not for professional competence, but for ideological loyalty. Its mandate was not to protect citizens from crime, but to protect the party from dissent. By 1934, the NKVD had become so powerful that it operated its own economy, running the Gulag system of forced labour camps that at its peak held over 1.5 million prisoners who produced timber, mined gold, and built canals with slave labour. The security service was not merely a department of the state. It was a state within a state, answering to no court, bound by no law, and accountable to no institution except the party leadership.  Second, the party captured the judiciary. Soviet courts did not administer justice; they administered policy. Judges were party members who received instructions, sometimes explicit, sometimes implicit, on the outcomes expected in politically sensitive cases. The concept of judicial independence did not exist. Andrey Vyshinsky, Stalin's chief prosecutor during the Great Purge, openly theorised that a confession was the "queen of evidence", and confessions were extracted through torture, sleep deprivation, and threats to family members. Between 1936 and 1938, the Soviet judiciary sentenced approximately 750,000 people to death, not through any process recognisable as law, but through show trials designed to demonstrate the party's absolute power over the lives of citizens. The courts were not captured gradually. They were designed from the beginning to serve the party. There was no independent judiciary to capture because the party never permitted one to exist.  Third, the party captured the economy. The Soviet command economy eliminated private enterprise, collectivised agriculture, and placed every factory, farm, mine, and shop under state, meaning party, control. The State Planning Committee (Gosplan) set production targets for the entire economy. Factory managers were party appointees who answered to party officials, not to markets, consumers, or shareholders. The result was an economy that could build nuclear weapons and launch satellites, but could not reliably produce bread, shoes, or toilet paper. By the 1980s, the Soviet economy was spending an estimated 15 to 17 per cent of GDP on defence while its citizens queued for basic consumer goods. The economy served the party's strategic objectives, including military power, ideological prestige, and geopolitical competition, rather than the material welfare of the people it claimed to represent.  Fourth, the party captured information. Pravda, the party newspaper whose name ironically means "Truth", was the instrument through which the party controlled what citizens knew about their own country and the world. Television, radio, publishing, and education were all party-controlled. The information ecosystem was not merely censored; it was manufactured. History was rewritten to serve current political needs. Photographs were altered to remove purged officials. Statistics were fabricated to demonstrate economic progress that did not exist. When the Chernobyl nuclear reactor exploded in April 1986, the Soviet state initially denied the disaster, delayed evacuations, and suppressed information about radiation levels because the party's image mattered more than the lives of citizens living in the fallout zone. The deep state did not merely hide the truth. It replaced the truth with a party-approved alternative reality and punished anyone who pointed out the difference.  The Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, not because it was invaded, and not because its military was defeated, but because the deep state it had built over seven decades had consumed the actual state. The institutions that should have sustained the country, such as the economy, the judiciary, the civil service, and the information systems, had been so thoroughly hollowed out by party capture that when the party lost legitimacy, there was nothing left to hold the country together. The state had been replaced by the party, and when the party fell, the state fell with it.  China under Mao Zedong followed the Soviet blueprint with Chinese characteristics, and with even more devastating consequences. The Great Leap Forward (1958–1962), in which the party ordered the collectivisation of agriculture and the rapid industrialisation of rural China, resulted in the deadliest famine in human history. Estimates range from 15 million to 55 million deaths. The famine was not caused by drought or natural disaster. It was caused by the deep state: by party officials at every level who fabricated grain production figures to please their superiors, who seized food from starving villages to meet impossible quotas, and who punished anyone who reported the truth. When Peng Dehuai, a senior military commander, privately told Mao that the Great Leap Forward was failing, he was purged, imprisoned, and tortured to death during the Cultural Revolution. The system did not merely fail to prevent the famine; the system caused the famine. The fusion of party and state meant that no institution existed to challenge the party's decisions, report accurate information, or protect citizens from the consequences of ideological insanity.  The Cultural Revolution (1966–1976) was the deep state turning on itself. Mao, fearing that the party bureaucracy had become too comfortable and too independent, unleashed the Red Guards, millions of radicalised young people, to attack the very institutions the party had built. Universities were closed. Teachers were beaten, humiliated, and killed. Scientists were sent to labour in rice paddies. Cultural artefacts were destroyed. Party officials who had served the revolution for decades were dragged through the streets, forced to wear dunce caps, and publicly denounced. An estimated 1.5 to 2 million people were killed. The Cultural Revolution demonstrated the ultimate danger of the deep state: when the party is the state, and the party leader decides the state itself is the enemy, there is no institution left to restrain the destruction.  China survived where the Soviet Union did not, but only by making a calculation that would have horrified Marx: it opened the economy to capitalism while keeping the party's monopoly on political power. Deng Xiaoping's reforms after 1978 created a hybrid system, specifically a market economy generating wealth, supervised by a one-party state that retained absolute control over the judiciary, the military, the media, and the security apparatus. China's economic miracle is real, but the deep state remains. The party controls the courts; there is no independent judiciary. The party controls the internet; the Great Firewall blocks information the party considers threatening. The party controls the military; the People's Liberation Army swears allegiance to the party, not to the state or the constitution. And when the party decides that an entire ethnic group poses a threat, the deep state delivers the machinery to intern over a million Uyghurs in camps in Xinjiang with no judicial oversight, no legal process, and no accountability. China's deep state did not disappear with economic reform. It adapted, and its capacity for control is now enhanced by surveillance technology that Stalin could not have imagined.  Cuba under Fidel Castro created a deep state so total that the country has been functionally frozen since 1959. The party controls every institution: the military, the judiciary, the media, the economy, the education system, and the security apparatus. The Committees for the Defence of the Revolution (CDRs), neighbourhood surveillance organisations established on every block of every city and town, ensured that the party's eyes and ears extended into every household. Citizens who expressed dissent were reported by their neighbours, investigated by state security, and imprisoned or exiled.  The result is a country that, despite having one of the highest literacy rates and best doctor-to-patient ratios in the developing world, cannot feed its population, provide basic consumer goods, maintain its infrastructure, or offer its young people any future other than emigration. Cuba's deep state did not fail through a dramatic collapse like that of the Soviet Union. It failed through stagnation: the slow, grinding degradation of a society in which no institution exists to challenge failed policies, no court exists to protect individual rights, and no mechanism exists for peaceful political change. Cuba's buildings are crumbling. Its cars are from the 1950s. Its economy runs on remittances from the diaspora that fled the revolution. The deep state preserved the party, but it destroyed the country the party claimed to serve.  The German Democratic Republic perfected the surveillance dimension of the communist deep state. The Stasi, the Ministry for State Security, employed approximately 91,000 full-time staff and maintained a network of an estimated 189,000 civilian informants in a country of only 16 million people. That means approximately one in every 63 East Germans was reporting on their neighbours, colleagues, friends, and family members to the state security apparatus.  The Stasi did not merely monitor dissidents; it monitored everyone. It opened mail. It tapped telephones. It bugged apartments. It infiltrated churches, universities, sports clubs, and cultural organisations. It developed a practice called Zersetzung ("decomposition"), in which it systematically destroyed the personal lives of targeted individuals through rumour campaigns, career sabotage, disruption of relationships, and psychological harassment, all without the target understanding that the state was responsible. The purpose was not to imprison dissidents; that was too visible. The purpose was to break them invisibly, from the inside.  When the Berlin Wall fell in November 1989, East Germans who accessed their Stasi files discovered that their spouses, their closest friends, and even their own children had been informing on them for years. The deep state had not merely surveilled the population; it had weaponised human relationships themselves, turning trust into a tool of state control. The psychological damage persists to this day, more than 35 years later. Former East Germans report lasting difficulties with trust, intimacy, and social cohesion, which represents the intergenerational trauma of a society in which the party made every human relationship a potential instrument of betrayal.  North Korea represents the final evolution of the communist deep state: a system so total that the distinction between party, state, and reality itself has been abolished. The Kim dynasty, Kim Il-sung, Kim Jong-il, and Kim Jong-un, has achieved what no other communist regime fully accomplished: the complete replacement of objective reality with a party-constructed reality.  North Koreans do not merely live under censorship. They live inside a manufactured universe in which the Kim family possesses supernatural qualities, in which North Korea is the most prosperous and powerful nation on earth, and in which the outside world is a hellscape of poverty, exploitation, and moral degeneracy. The state controls every source of information: there is no internet, no foreign media, no independent publishing, and no uncensored communication with the outside world. Citizens who are discovered consuming foreign media, even South Korean television dramas, face imprisonment in political prison camps, where an estimated 80,000 to 120,000 people are held in conditions the United Nations has compared to Nazi concentration camps.  The deep state in North Korea does not serve any ideology, not even communism, which the regime effectively abandoned decades ago in favour of Juche (self-reliance) and Songun (military-first) doctrines. It serves only the perpetuation of the Kim family's rule. The military consumes an estimated 15 to 24 per cent of GDP while periodic famines kill tens of thousands. The party maintains control through a classification system called Songbun that assigns every citizen to one of three loyalty categories (core, wavering, or hostile) based on the political history of their ancestors. Your grandfather's political reliability in the 1950s determines your access to food, education, housing, and employment today. The deep state does not merely control the present. It has retroactively colonised the past, making every family's history a permanent political verdict from which there is no appeal.  The Khmer Rouge under Pol Pot demonstrated the most extreme consequence of the communist deep state: the point at which the party's capture of the state becomes indistinguishable from the extermination of the population. Between 1975 and 1979, the Khmer Rouge emptied Cambodia's cities, abolished money, closed schools and hospitals, destroyed temples, executed intellectuals, and attempted to create an agrarian utopia through forced labour. An estimated 1.5 to 2 million people, approximately 25 per cent of Cambodia's population, died from execution, starvation, disease, and forced labour.  The deep state under the Khmer Rouge was not bureaucratic. It was eliminationist. The party decided that the existing state, society, and population were all contaminated by capitalism, imperialism, and bourgeois values, and therefore all had to be destroyed and rebuilt from zero. The security apparatus, centred on the S-21 interrogation centre at Tuol Sleng, tortured and executed approximately 17,000 people, including many of the party's own cadres, in a spiralling paranoia of purges that consumed the revolution from within. The deep state's final act was to devour itself, executing its own members on suspicion of disloyalty until the party that had destroyed a quarter of its nation's population began destroying its own leadership.  Every communist deep state, including the Soviet, Chinese, Cuban, East German, North Korean, and Cambodian regimes, followed the same structural logic.  The party captures the security services so that the instruments of force serve the party rather than the law. The party captures the judiciary so that courts deliver political outcomes rather than justice. The party captures the economy so that citizens depend on the party for their livelihoods and cannot build independent economic power. The party captures information so that citizens cannot access the facts they need to evaluate the party's performance. The party captures education so that the next generation is socialised into loyalty rather than critical thinking. And the party captures human relationships themselves, through neighbourhood committees, informant networks, and the weaponisation of trust, so that citizens cannot organise, confide, or build the social solidarity that collective action requires.  The result, in every case, is the same: a state that serves the party rather than the people; an economy that produces what the party wants rather than what the people need; a judiciary that punishes the party's enemies rather than protecting the people's rights; a security apparatus that monitors the people rather than defending them; and an information environment in which the party's version of reality replaces actual reality, until the gap between the two becomes so vast that the system collapses under the weight of its own lies.  Sri Lanka is not a communist country. The NPP/JVP government does not propose to abolish private enterprise, collectivise agriculture, or establish a one-party state. But the JVP's roots are Marxist-Leninist. Its founder, Rohana Wijeweera, was trained in Moscow. Its two insurrections, in 1971 and 1987–1989, attempted to seize the state by force. And the organisational instincts of the party, namely the discipline, the hierarchy, the suspicion of dissent, the conflation of party interests with national interests, and the treatment of critics as enemies rather than citizens, carry the DNA of the movements that built the deep states described above.  When the CIABOC Director General is identified as a former JVP legal division member, that is not a neutral staffing decision. It is the party placing its people inside the state's anti-corruption machinery. When four Supreme Court vacancies are left unfilled while sitting judges' tenures are extended by government legislation, that is the party shaping the judiciary to its advantage. When the CID questions journalists about their tweets, contacts social media platforms to demand content removal, and intelligence officers threaten citizens who participate in UN reviews, that is the party using the state's security apparatus to monitor and silence critics. When pro-government thugs break up an independent farmers' conference, that is the party using extra-state violence to suppress organizing that the party cannot control. When the Agriculture Minister calls protesting farmers "kasippu drinkers," that is the party demonstrating contempt for citizens who challenge its authority.  None of these individual acts constitutes a communist deep state. But taken together, they describe a trajectory: the gradual, incremental fusion of party and state that every communist regime began with before it metastasised into something far worse. The Soviet Union did not start with the Gulag. It started with staffing decisions, loyalty tests, the placement of party members in key institutional positions, the harassment of critics, and the conflation of dissent and treason. The Gulag came later, after the institutions that could have prevented it had already been captured.  The people of Sri Lanka do not need to wait for the Gulag to recognise the pattern. They need to recognise it now: while the institutions that protect them still exist, while the judiciary still has some independence, while the media can still report, while citizens can still organise, while elections still happen, and while the line between government and state has been blurred but not yet erased. Because every country that waited until the line was fully erased discovered the same truth: by then, there was nothing left to fight with, no institution left to appeal to, and no mechanism left for peaceful change. The deep state had consumed the state. And the people, the people in whose name the revolution was always conducted, had nothing left but the party's version of reality and the party's definition of freedom.  That is the lesson of every communist deep state: not that communism attracts bad people, but that the fusion of party and state, regardless of the intentions behind it, inevitably produces a system that serves the party at the expense of the people. Sri Lanka must decide now, not later, whether it will permit that fusion to continue or whether it will defend the independence of the institutions that belong to its citizens, not to any party. The answer to that question will determine whether Sri Lanka remains a democracy with problems or becomes another cautionary tale in the long, bloody history of states that were consumed by the parties that claimed to serve them.  #SriLanka #LKA #DeepState #JVP #NPP

Those amazing and heroic Israelis  An averted catastrophe in the air shows how the Jewish state chooses life, while Britain and the West are embracing a culture of death.  On Monday, Britain’s foreign secretary Ed Miliband delivered a diatribe against Israel, accusing it of ethnic cleansing and war crimes, and vowing to punish it for the crime of allowing Jews to “settle” in their own historic land.  On Wednesday, four ordinary Israelis on a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv averted a new 9/11 by overpowering the co-pilot who was attempting to crash the plane, possibly in Israel.  There could hardly be a better illustration of the way Britain is now choosing to embrace a culture of death while Israel is choosing life.  When they heard an alarming commotion in the cockpit, a small handful of Israeli passengers jumped out of their seats and burst in to see the Omani co-pilot stabbing the captain.  One of the Israelis, a plumber by trade, got the assailant in a chokehold. As other Israeli passengers and Emirati crew members helped tie the terrorist up, the plumber seized the control stick and pulled the plane out of its lethal dive.  When Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, asked him afterwards how he’d known what to do, he replied that he’d seen it done on a TV show.  Only the Israelis could behave like this—regular people displaying raw courage, heroism and the lion-hearted, can-do Israeli spirit.   Alerted to an existential threat, these ordinary guys immediately took matters into their own hands, neutralized the danger and saved countless lives.  What an amazing, wonderful, heroic country.   What a symbol of everything Israel has been doing for the past three years, ever since Hamas launched its genocidal onslaught against it on Oct. 7, 2023.  What a statement of defiance against Britain and a Western world now consumed (whatever they think they’re supporting) by a deranged agenda to wipe this country out.  How this lifts the spirits.   And how those spirits are instantly lowered by contact with the life-destroying venom of the Western intelligentsia.  Western media outlets tried everything they could to downplay the near-catastrophe in the skies over Saudi Arabia.  CNN called it “an internal personnel incident between pilots.” The New York Times called it “a clash in the cockpit.” Reuters headlined it: “A pilot brawl, then a rapid descent: Passengers recount chaos in flydubai flight.”  As ever, the BBC excelled itself as a disgrace to journalism. BBC News reported: “Israel’s far right national security minister Ben-Gvir says that an Israel bound flight that landed in Saudi Arabia was due to a terrorist who wanted to crash the plane and kill Israelis.”  By pointlessly singling out the left’s principal Israeli bogeyman as its source of information, the BBC primed its audience to believe that the Israelis must be assumed to be lying because they are political extremists.  A new order is being born in which Arabs and Jews are fighting together against the forces of barbarism in the Islamic world.  Remarkably, a BBC reporter subsequently referred to Israel’s Ben-Gurion International Airport as “Ben-Gvir airport”—a slip of the mind, perhaps, but all-too revealing about the state of that BBC mind.  On Thursday, a BBC News headline ran: “Too early to say what motive for Dubai-Tel Aviv flight attack was, Israeli PM says.”  No, he didn’t. Netanyahu made it clear that intelligence confirmed it was a terror attack and merely said it was too early to tell whether Iran had been involved.  In other words, the BBC grossly misreported what he had said.  Such wicked distortions by the media reflect a far wider pathology.   Left-wingers simply can’t process the fact that Israelis may be targeted for destruction by the Palestinian Arabs or act courageously to defend themselves.  jns.org/opinion/column/melan…

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Full Compromise of Sri Lanka Police e-Services System  A darkweb forum post alleges that the electronic services system of the Sri Lanka Police, specifically the security clearance certificate issuance platform hosted on eservicespolice.lk, has been completely compromised. The actor claims to have gained full access to the server infrastructure, including root privileges on the Linux operating system, the MySQL database, and the WildFly 902Final application server. The post asserts that this breach exposes the personal data of citizens and residents of Sri Lanka to significant risk.  According to the listing, the attacker stole a wide array of sensitive configuration and application files from the server directory. Key artifacts allegedly exfiltrated include:  *   **Configuration Files:** application-users.properties (containing usernames and encrypted passwords for the ClearanceCertificate application), mgmt-users.properties, mgmt-groups.properties, and standalone.xml. *   **Application Archives:** ClearanceCertificate.war (a 35 MB file containing source code) and wildfly-902Final-2026-08-24-New-DB-Conn.tar.gz (a 595 MB backup). *   **System Logs:** A 17 GB nohup.out runtime log, .bash_history, .mysql_history, and SSH keys located in the .ssh directory.  The post further details that the system uses OAuth for authentication and processes credit card payments of 5,000 Sri Lankan rupees for security clearance applications. The actor claims that error logs and temporary files reveal potential password leaks and indicate that the system remains operational despite the vulnerabilities. Additionally, the thread includes an advertisement for a tool to exploit CVE-2017-5638, a critical Apache Struts2 vulnerability that allows remote command execution without authentication, suggesting the method used or available for exploitation.  The Sri Lanka Police is the primary law enforcement agency in the country, responsible for maintaining public order and investigating crimes. While the specific size of the database is not quantified in the post, the compromise of a national-level government service handling citizen identity verification and financial transactions represents a high-severity incident if verified. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the Sri Lankan government or security researchers.

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Massive Breach of Multiple Indian Government Agencies  A threat actor operating under the alias 'Bytetobreach' has posted a claim on an underground forum alleging the compromise of multiple Indian government entities and healthcare providers. The post is PGP-signed, indicating an attempt to verify the author's identity within the underground community. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the Indian government or the mentioned organizations. The claims involve high-profile targets, including state-level administration and critical healthcare infrastructure, which would constitute a significant security incident if authentic. 🚨 Threat Actor Claims 11M Record Breach of Transfast/Mastercard Database  A post on an underground forum alleges the compromise of a database belonging to Transfast, a global cross-border payments network provider acquired by Mastercard in July 2019. The threat actor claims to have exfiltrated approximately 11 million records from the company's systems. The listing includes a sample of the data, which appears to consist of SMS notification logs generated by Transfast's payment infrastructure.  The exposed data fields in the sample include sequential IDs, usernames, creation dates, originating and destination addresses (phone numbers), country of destination, mobile network operator details, and the content of the SMS messages. The messages indicate standard transactional notifications, such as "Your money is ready for collection" or "Your money is transferred to the bank," sent to recipients in countries including the Philippines, India, Pakistan, Bahrain, Jordan, Oman, and Kenya.  Transfast operates as a critical component of Mastercard's global payment ecosystem, facilitating cross-border money transfers and remittances. While the specific nature of the breach whether it involved direct access to customer financial accounts or merely the notification gateway is not explicitly detailed beyond the sample data, the exposure of phone numbers and transaction statuses could facilitate targeted social engineering or phishing campaigns against customers.  At the time of reporting, neither Transfast nor Mastercard has publicly confirmed the incident, and the authenticity of the leaked data has not been independently verified.

🤖⚠️ INTERPOL CISO: AI IS SPEEDING UP CYBER THREATS — AGENTIC AI CAN CAUSE REAL-WORLD HARM  Bjorn R. Watne, Interpol’s global chief information security officer, sat down with CNBC’s Jenny Lee on the sidelines of Tech Week Singapore.  The takeaway is clear:  AI is an EVOLUTION of existing criminal tactics — not a revolution.  What changes is SPEED and SCALE.  Watne said scam operators can now use AI to hit MANY victims at once. Better translation and digital identities are blurring the line between fraud and real interactions.  On defense, he urged companies to identify their “crown jewels” — the assets that keep operations running — and tailor protections to WHO would actually target them.  “There is no need for everyone to try and protect against everything all at once when they’re not being targeted by it.”  The sharper warning is about AGENTIC AI.  When AI only feeds wrong information, the risk is limited.  When AI ACTS for users — including in cars and self-driving systems — wrong actions can cause BODILY HARM, not just bad answers.  Watne also flagged over-trust in technology versus the control mindset people bring to financial safeguards (PINs, card skimming awareness).  “When it comes to technology, the trust level is through the roof.”  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is a CNBC interview with Interpol’s global CISO — NOT a report that Interpol was breached or cyberattacked. The URL slug is misleading; the story is threat-outlook commentary on AI-enabled crime and agentic-action risk. 🚨 CRITICAL FLAWS COULD TURN PHYSICAL ACCESS-CONTROL SYSTEMS AGAINST THEIR OPERATORS  CISA has disclosed a serious vulnerability chain affecting:  ARMATURA ONE  The platform is used to centrally manage physical security and access-control environments.  Affected deployments exist across:  * Energy * Transportation * Communications * Critical manufacturing  And the vulnerabilities cross the boundary between CYBER and PHYSICAL SECURITY.  CISA says successful exploitation could allow an attacker to:  * Access the application's database * Execute arbitrary code with the HIGHEST host privileges * Obtain sensitive credentials * Potentially gain control of the PHYSICAL ACCESS-CONTROL SYSTEM  Five vulnerabilities are involved:  * CVE-2023-46604 * CVE-2026-94591 * CVE-2026-94592 * CVE-2026-94593 * CVE-2026-94594  The most severe issue comes from an embedded Apache ActiveMQ component.  Its OpenWire listener is exposed on the network by default and is affected by CVE-2023-46604:  CVSS 9.8  An unauthenticated network attacker can potentially trigger deserialization BEFORE authentication and execute arbitrary code with the highest privileges of the host OS.  But CISA found several additional security-design problems:  * Hard-coded AES encryption key + initialization vector * Vendor-defined database SUPERUSER password * Database credentials written into plaintext logs * Message-broker credentials exposed in logs  ⚠️ Important distinction:  CVE-2023-46604 is a known-exploited vulnerability in other environments, but CISA says it is NOT currently aware of public exploitation specifically targeting Armatura One.  Still, the potential consequence here is unusual.  Compromise isn't limited to stealing data or gaining a shell.  The vulnerable application sits in the control plane for PHYSICAL ACCESS.  Affected organizations should upgrade to:  * Armatura One 4.7.2 * Armatura One USA 4.6.1_USA  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  Physical-security management platforms deserve the same isolation assumptions as OT.  When one server controls identities, doors and access permissions, a software compromise can stop being purely digital.  The final target may be the BUILDING.  cisa.gov/news-events/ics-adv… #ICS #OTSecurity #PhysicalSecurity #CISA #CriticalInfrastructure #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntel #DDW

🤖🚨 OPENAI DISRUPTS 15,000-USER CAMPAIGN TRYING TO EXTRACT HIDDEN AI REASONING  OpenAI has disclosed a large-scale operation designed to extract the protected reasoning of its AI models.  The activity is consistent with:  ADVERSARIAL DISTILLATION  OpenAI identified related activity across a cluster of more than:  15,000 USERS.  A core cluster was attributed by OpenAI to individuals associated with:  MOONSHOT AI  the Chinese AI company behind Kimi.  The operation began July 1.  Then activity surged.  On July 24–25 alone, OpenAI detected:  * 16,000 extraction-pattern requests * More than 4,000 users involved  One technique was particularly interesting.  Operators copied ENCRYPTED REASONING from one conversation and attempted to get a model in another conversation to:  DECRYPT + TRANSCRIBE IT.  Independent researchers also discovered related cross-model and conversation-compaction vulnerabilities.  OpenAI investigated those findings and confirmed the attack paths were REAL.  The company has now closed a pathway where someone who already possessed another user's encrypted reasoning could replay it and recover its contents.  Important distinction:  * OpenAI says attackers did NOT break its encryption * They did NOT compromise an OpenAI database * They did NOT gain direct access to stored user conversations  Instead, they manipulated model interactions to reproduce protected reasoning in requester-visible forms.  OpenAI says the broader campaign was fully disrupted by July 28.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  Model theft is evolving beyond stealing weights or API outputs.  Protected reasoning itself is becoming a HIGH-VALUE TARGET.  At scale, extracting reasoning can help another model reproduce capabilities without paying the same training, research and safety costs.  There is also a security consequence:  A distilled model could inherit advanced capabilities WITHOUT inheriting the original model's safeguards.  OpenAI explicitly warns that this becomes increasingly relevant as frontier models gain capabilities in dual-use domains.  This may become the AI equivalent of intellectual-property theft combined with capability proliferation.  openai.com/index/disrupting-… #OpenAI #MoonshotAI #Kimi #AISecurity #AI #ModelSecurity #ThreatIntel #DDW

Test anxiety is not a distinct mental condition, but the normal nervousness humans have before anything with stakes to it -- a test, a speech, a driving test, a conversation with your boss. Some students are more nervous than others, that's okay. But the push to classify this natural nervousness as a distinct condition known as "test anxiety" that requires accommodations has been widely harmful and counterproductive.  Humans manage their nervousness in all sectors of life, they must learn to manage it in school also. We should teach them how to prepare properly.  A counterargument I always see is that students have this "anxiety" because we make the stakes on these tests too high.  But to that I say: A class final exam or the SAT is not the end of the world and not "too high stakes", but by giving students superfluous accommodations on the test like 2x time, infinite extensions, or retakes, you are actually sending the message that it is more important than it is.  The message is that it's SO important for you to score well on this test we will do anything to make it easier for you to score higher, even destroy any shred of academic integrity.

Only a tiny fraction of the world’s mosquito species prey on humans. All of these are invasive across essentially their entire range, having tagged along with humans as we moved around the world. Multiple careful studies say that eliminating these species would have little or no impact on the environment. However, it would save at least a million human lives a year, and get rid of a constant source of discomfort that prevents people from safely spending as much time outside as they would prefer. Malaria is only one of dozens of diseases, many potentially fatal, spread by mosquitoes. Gene drives can safely and relatively inexpensively eliminate these parasitic insects; we can create male mosquitoes that can only have male offspring and which then crash the population. It’s well past time that we did it.

Let me tell you how I delayed WinXP SP2 for a month.  My software (BlackICE) was on the list of software that had to work. When they made major changes to the kernel network stack, my software broke.  They grabbed their reverse engineers to figure out why. What they discovered was that my software doing something evil, patching the kernel's network stack when our software was loaded. That's tricky on a multi-CPU system with warring instruction/data caches. We wrote a patent on how to do it reliably without crashing the system.  We searched through the kernel to find the location we needed to patch, looking for a certain pattern of bytes. They changed the network stack so that thing we were patching no longer existed.  So to make our software work, the inserted that pattern back into the kernel. As packets arrived, the new function would jump to that pattern, and then after, jump right back. This way, we could find the pattern and patch it -- and thereby patch the intended function.  Some Microsoft lawyers wanted to sue us for violating the software license agreement, which forbids reverse engineering, which we had to do in order to patch the kernel at runtime.  Cooler heads prevailed.  The point is our software did an ugly hack in order to work, and then Microsoft did an even crazier, uglier hack so that we'd keep working.  For years after, when meeting Microsoft engineers at conferences, they'd love to yell at me.  When Vista came along, they added signing of kernel models, putting an end to such nonsense, but also providing a real documented API we could use.

🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-10-03 09:59 KST
🔴 위협 점수: 2026/10 (심각)

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협은 AI 기술을 악용한 자동화된 공격과 오픈소스 공급망 공격이 결합되어 더욱 정교해지고 있습니다. 특히 GitLab AI Gateway와 같은 AI 인프라의 취약점을 노린 RCE 공격이 급증하고 있으며, 공격자들은 기존의 전통적인 기법 대신 신뢰받는 협업 도구나 API 권한 검증 허점을 파고드는 방식을 선호합니다 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/gitlab-patches-critical-self-hosted-ai.html)). 또한, 보안 팀의 대응 속도를 앞지르는 'Machine-Speed' 공격에 대응하기 위해 자율 방어 플랫폼과 AI 기반의 위협 탐지 체계 도입이 필수적인 과제로 떠오르고 있습니다 ([Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/autonomous-defense-platform)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **Warlock**: SharePoint 취약점을 악용하여 수자원, 통신사, 대학 등 공공 및 교육 인프라를 타겟팅하는 중국 연계 랜섬웨어 그룹 ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/warlock-ransomware-breach-sharepoint-in-water-telecom-operator-attacks/)).
- **Antino**: Outlook과 OneDrive를 C2 채널로 활용하여 아시아 지역 정부 및 정책 기관을 대상으로 스파이 활동을 수행하는 중국 연계 그룹 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/antino-backdoor-uses-outlook-and.html)).
- **KillSec**: 2년 미만의 기간 동안 약 500개 조직을 공격한 10대 중심의 갈취 그룹으로, 최근 인프라가 압수되고 핵심 멤버가 체포됨 ([CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/killsec-ransomware-group-arrests-operation-killswitch/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **금융권 AI 자율 침투 공격**: 신한은행을 포함한 국내 금융권에서 AI 자율 침투 도구를 이용한 API 권한 검증 허점 공격이 발생하여 고객 정보 유출 사고가 이어지고 있음 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208718)).
- **카카오톡 사칭 악성코드**: SEO Poisoning을 통해 카카오톡 설치 파일로 위장한 악성코드가 국내 유포 중이며, NSIS/Advanced Installer 등을 순차적으로 사용하는 변종이 확인됨 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95641/)).
- **통신/메일 게이트웨이 타겟팅**: BPFDoor, Rekoobe, AVERAT 등의 악성코드가 한국과 대만의 통신 에지 장비 및 메일 보안 게이트웨이를 공격 중 ([DFIR_Radar](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2106022326546657725)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-90970**: GitLab AI Gateway RCE, CVSS 9.9, 즉시 업데이트 권고 ([iss_kk_official](https://twitter.com/iss_kk_official/status/2106180163675594821)).
- **CVE-2026-104286**: FortiMail Path Traversal/Arbitrary File Write, CVSS 9.8, 실제 악용 중 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)).
- **CVE-2026-63292**: Apache HTTP Server RCE, CVSS 9.8, 패치 적용 필요 ([Netlas_io](https://twitter.com/Netlas_io/status/2105937851904938488)).
- **CVE-2026-61821**: PostgreSQL pg_partman Privilege Escalation, CVSS 8.5, 즉시 업데이트 권고 ([DFIR_Lab](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Lab/status/2106183780088111316)).
- **CVE-2026-61818**: PostgreSQL pg_partman SQL Injection, CVSS 8.5, 즉시 업데이트 권고 ([DFIR_Lab](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Lab/status/2106178756649881988)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-63688 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/dell-csm-flaws-enable-unauthenticated.html)), CVE-2026-88771/88772 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)), CVE-2025-39682/53266/39964 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5781)).

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **GitLab AI Gateway 점검**: Self-Hosted 환경의 AI Gateway를 최신 버전(19.2.4/19.3.2/19.4.1)으로 즉시 업데이트하십시오.
- **FortiMail 보안 강화**: CVE-2026-104286 대응을 위해 관리자 페이지의 외부 노출을 즉시 차단하고, 시스템 파일 변조 여부를 점검하십시오.
- **금융/공공 API 보안 감사**: AI 자율 침투 공격에 대비하여 API 권한 검증 로직을 재검토하고, 비정상적인 대량 데이터 접근 로그를 모니터링하십시오.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
- **점수**: 9/10
- **근거**: AI 인프라 및 에지 보안 장비의 제로데이 취약점이 실제 공격에 활발히 악용되고 있으며, 국내 금융권을 포함한 주요 인프라가 직접적인 타겟이 되고 있음.
